subtopics.title: 1.1 Exploring the context of a design

outcomes.text: Explore where and how a product or system is used.
Identify the requirements of the primary user and wider stakeholders.
Investigate social, cultural, moral and economic factors to spot opportunities and constraints.
Explain how a solution affects a user's lifestyle.
Judge ease of use and inclusivity of a design.
Use ergonomics and anthropometric data to support ease of use.
Consider aesthetics in a design.

topics.title: 2. Learning from existing products and practice

outcomes.text: Identify the materials, components and processes used in an existing product.
Explain the influence of fashion, trends, taste and style, and of marketing and branding.
Assess a product's impact on society, usability and the environment, including life cycle assessment.
Describe the work of past and present professionals and companies in design and technology.
Evaluate how new and emerging technologies influence design decisions, now and in future, in terms of ethics, environment and product enhancement.

subtopics.title: 3.1 Impacts of new and emerging technologies

outcomes.text: Explore impacts on industry and enterprise, such as the circular economy.
Explore impacts on people's lifestyle, culture and society.
Explore impacts on the environment and on sustainability.
Explain how electricity is generated and energy stored and transferred.
Compare fossil fuels, nuclear fuel and biofuel as non-renewable or other sources.
Compare wind, hydroelectric, tidal and solar renewable sources for products and systems.

subtopics.title: 3.3 Wider influences on designing and making

outcomes.text: Explain environmental initiatives and fair trade.
Explain social and ethical awareness and global sustainable development.
Use clear 2D and 3D sketches with notes, sketch modelling and exploded drawings.
Use mathematical modelling and flow charts to communicate ideas and technical considerations.
Describe user-centred design and systems thinking.
Explain why collaboration across subject areas brings specialist knowledge to solutions.
Explain that products are mainly made from several materials.
Describe papers and boards: papers, card, boards and sheets, and laminated layers.
Describe hardwoods, softwoods and manufactured boards.
Describe ferrous metals, non-ferrous metals and alloys.
Describe thermo polymers and thermosetting polymers.
Describe natural, synthetic and blended fibres, and woven, non-woven and knitted fabrics.
Know developments in modern and smart materials, composites and technical textiles.
Describe properties of the main material categories (density, strength, hardness, durability, elasticity, conductivity and more) and why they suit different uses.
Judge the physical and working properties of specific materials and how easy they are to work with.
Weigh function, aesthetics, environment, availability, cost, and social, cultural and ethical factors when selecting materials.
Know the sources and origins of specific materials and components.
Give an overview of how source materials are extracted and converted into workable form.
Discuss ecological, social and ethical issues in mining, harvesting, manufacturing and transport.
Explain the life cycle of materials in products.
Explain recycling, reuse, disposal, eco-materials and upcycling.

subtopics.title: 5.4 Available forms of materials and components

outcomes.text: Know commonly available weights, sizes and stock forms such as lengths, sheets, pellets, reels and rods.
Know standard components for paper, timber, metals, polymers and fabrics.
Know standard system components (resistors, capacitors, diodes, transistors, microcontrollers) and mechanical components (gears, cams, pulleys, levers).
Explain why materials and components are reinforced or stiffened to withstand forces and stresses.
Describe triangulation, boning, darts, layering, plastic webbing and reinforcing.
Describe finishes and surface treatments for function, such as durability and resistance to the environment.
Describe finishes and surface treatments for aesthetics.
Describe rotary, linear, oscillating and reciprocating motion.
Explain how load, effort and fulcrum affect ease of movement.
Explain how cams, gears, pulleys and belts, levers and linkages change the size and direction of motion or force.
Describe sensors such as LDRs and infra-red sensors, and switches such as tilt, push-to-make and time-delay.
Describe outputs: LEDs for light, speakers and buzzers for sound, and motors for motion.
Explain how programmable components such as microcontrollers embed and customise functionality.
Describe processes and techniques for producing early models and toiles that support iterative design.

subtopics.title: 7.2 Shaping and joining in a workshop

outcomes.text: Describe wastage processes for papers, timber, metals, polymers, fabrics and design engineering.
Describe addition processes such as adhesion, joining, welding, riveting, sewing and soldering.
Describe deforming and reforming processes such as folding, steaming, bending, casting, moulding and pleating.
Use measuring, reference points, lines and surfaces to mark out accurately.
Use templates, jigs and patterns, and work within tolerances.
Cut efficiently to minimise waste.
Describe how 2D and 3D digital tools present, model, design and manufacture solutions, such as rapid prototyping, CAD, CAM and CAE.
Interpret plans and elevations of 3D models and use image software.
Compare one-off, batch and mass production.
Explain lean manufacturing and just-in-time methods.
Know large-scale processes for papers and boards, timber and metals.
Know large-scale processes for polymers, fabrics and design engineering, including laser cutting and 3D printing.
Evaluate benefits and implications of new technologies in production, including economies of scale and disruptive technologies like 3D printing and robotics.
Explain how material and component cost affects commercial viability, stakeholder needs and marketability.
Calculate quantities, costs and sizes of materials and components required.

units.title: Mathematical skills in the Principles exam

topics.title: Maths skills in design and technology

outcomes.text: Use decimal and standard form with metric units for quantities, cost and sizes.
Use ratios to scale drawings and fractions and percentages for data, profit and waste.
Calculate surface area and volume of cuboids and composite shapes, applying tolerances.

subtopics.title: M2 and M3 Data and graphs

outcomes.text: Construct and interpret frequency tables, pie charts, bar charts and histograms.
Plot, draw and interpret graphs, and translate between graphical and numeric information.
Use angles in degrees, triangle properties, basic trigonometry and symmetry for accurate marking out and tessellation.
Visualise and draw 2D and 3D forms, including isometric drawings.
Calculate areas of triangles and rectangles and surface areas and volumes of cuboids, including scale factors.
